clue.text: Could be fine position for hostile attack

indicators.note: the letters of fine could be something else once reshuffled

parts.note: a station is a post or position someone is assigned to

explanation.surface: A good vantage point might be ideal for launching an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' is the anagram signal working on 'fine'; 'for' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm of pests overrunning a place is an invasion, an assault by unwelcome creatures.

clue.text: Send off, enclosing note, for what you require

indicators.note: the jumbled word wraps round the musical note
off signals the letters of send are thrown out of order

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: Dispatch something with a memo attached because you must have it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns SEND into NEDS; 'enclosing' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Requirements are necessities, the things one must have.

clue.text: Similar spirit in upbringing proving puzzling

definitions.note: noun phrase sense: things that prove puzzling

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
the spirit sits inside the word for similar

parts.note: similar things are the same
gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: Children raised alike with drink in the home turn out baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts GIN into SAME making SAGINME... precisely SAM-GIN-E, and 'upbringing' turns SAMGINE upwards. The definition is loose: plural mysteries are things proving puzzling.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddles and mysteries are things that baffle, so they prove puzzling.

clue.text: But would this blade be so reliable if the top came off?

definitions.text: But would this blade be so reliable if the top came off?

parts.words: But would this blade be so reliable if the top came off?
parts.note: a corroded knife is not dependable, and the word for dependable loses its first letter to give the word for corroded

explanation.surface: A doubt about whether a blade stays dependable once its tip breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first letter (the top, in a down entry) and the word becomes RUSTY: a rusty blade would hardly be reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependable, faithful thing can be relied on, like an old trusted friend.

clue.text: Partly covering. the trunk of this tree

indicators.note: of in the sense of made from, so the answer is fashioned from the letters of this tree

explanation.surface: A description of bark wrapping part of a tree's trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' (made out of) rearranges THIS TREE into the eight letters needed. 'Trunk' looks botanical but means the human torso, which the garment partly covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sleeved casual top covers the upper body but leaves arms exposed.

clue.text: Romans at sea with captured English galley-slaves

indicators.note: the jumble takes in the abbreviation as a prisoner
at sea means confused, so the letters of Romans are jumbled

explanation.surface: Romans sailing with English prisoners chained to the oars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns ROMANS into OARSMN; 'captured' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Galley slaves were rowers forced to pull the oars of ancient warships.

clue.text: Insect on motor-cyclist's back?

definitions.meaning: the larva of the crane fly, a garden pest
the garment a biker typically wears

explanation.surface: A bug landing on a biker's back.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane-fly grub shares its name with the hide garment bikers wear on their backs.

clue.text: Guy allows wreaths

parts.note: a guy is a chap, a man
allows means lets

explanation.surface: A man permits floral garlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlands worn on the head are circlets of flowers or leaves.

clue.text: Coming to river, not entirely keen on taking risks

parts.note: an advent is a coming or arrival
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
some is part rather than all

explanation.surface: Arriving at the river, someone is only partly eager to gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' gives SOME, as in some but not all.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring and bold people relish adventure and danger.

clue.text: Inserting point in tree I thus obtain resin

indicators.note: inserting means putting the point inside the tree

parts.note: an elm is a tree
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Tapping a tree is how one gets its sap.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant gum from tropical trees, used in varnishes and ointments.

clue.text: Perhaps a shocking thing to have dug up

definitions.meaning: an appliance lacking an earth connection may give an electric shock

explanation.surface: Something alarming discovered when digging.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrically it means lacking an earth wire; in general it means excavated.

clue.text: Trial marriage?

parts.note: read as a trial plus a marriage, it describes an international cricket fixture

explanation.surface: A couple living together before wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Test = trial and match = marriage; together they name an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: An international cricket fixture over several days is literally a test plus a match.

clue.text: Ample source of sugar

parts.note: a tree whose sap gives syrup, whose name rearranges the letters of Ample

explanation.surface: A plentiful supply of sweetness.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an anagram of AMPLE, though no word signals it; the tree's sap is boiled into syrup and sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: This Canadian tree's sap is tapped to make syrup and sugar.

clue.text: Russian returns to point of departure

indicators.note: returns means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Serge is a Russian man's name
S is a compass point, south

explanation.surface: A Russian goes back to where he set off from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns SERGE into EGRES. 'Point of departure' looks like the definition, but 'point' supplies S and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit or going out is a leaving, a way out.

clue.text: Wanderer around city area may end by getting rehabilitation

indicators.note: the wanderer goes round the city area

parts.note: a rover is a wanderer
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: end picks the last letter of may

explanation.surface: A drifter loitering in town may finally get back on his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting back to health is restoration, a return to a sound state.

clue.text: Controversial patterns in church building

indicators.note: controversial suggests disputed or disturbed, so the letters of patterns are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disputed designs found in an ecclesiastical building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Controversial' rearranges PATTERNS. The definition is a part of a church, the crosswise arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-arm of a cruciform church is part of its structure.

clue.text: Jack-of-all-trades utilizing Manx tom-cat fur

indicators.note: utilizing the letters means making something new out of them
a Manx cat has no tail, so the phrase loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A handyman makes use of the coat of a tailless cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' (the tailless cat breed) cuts R from TOMCATFUR; 'utilizing' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A general servant or handyman does every kind of task.

clue.text: Girl riding a horse in bygone times

definitions.note: adjective phrase: belonging to an earlier period

indicators.note: riding means sitting astride, here with the horse held inside the girl's name

parts.note: Jean is a girl's name
a cob is a sturdy horse

explanation.surface: A girl on horseback in olden days.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to the reign of James I, an era long past.

clue.text: This bird pecked another

parts.note: pecked means bit
another bird, a tern, a seabird

explanation.surface: One bird attacked another with its beak.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading heron known for its booming call.

clue.text: Make a mistake over a couple of points but get the rubber

indicators.note: the word for blunder goes over and around the other letters

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
S and E are two compass points

explanation.surface: Errors over a pair of decimal places are fixed with a correction tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the container signal: the word for a blunder sits over, wrapping round, A and two compass points. 'Rubber' is the British word for a pencil eraser.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a rubber is the tool that rubs out pencil marks.

clue.text: Call again about six, bearing object

parts.note: re means about, concerning
VI is six in Roman numerals
S, south, is a compass bearing
it is an object pronoun, a thing

explanation.surface: A return phone call at six o'clock about something.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back to a place is to pay a further visit there.

clue.text: Does not go yet in the long run keeps going

definitions.meaning: one who stays on rather than leaving

definitions.text: in the long run keeps going
definitions.meaning: a horse or runner with stamina over long distances

explanation.surface: Someone who lingers and endures.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who remains rather than leaving; also a racehorse with stamina for long races.

clue.text: Indulge in wishful thinking?

parts.note: to long for what belongs to someone else

explanation.surface: Daydreaming about what might be.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave or yearn for something, especially another's possession.

clue.text: Bird doctor is a vet and brings about improvements

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of is a vet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small bird treated by a veterinarian gets better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' rearranges ISAVET into IVATES. 'Doctor' looks like a noun beside 'vet' but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To spruce up or smarten something makes it look better.

clue.text: Trunk that's lifeless-roots damaged

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of roots are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dead tree with spoiled roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges ROOTS. 'Trunk' suggests a tree, but it is a sculpture of the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue of the human trunk without head or limbs is a lifeless body.

clue.text: Bird most likely to find worms-circles nest with assiduity

indicators.note: circles means the word goes round the nest

parts.words: Bird most likely to find worms
parts.note: the early bird catches the worm, as the proverb says
taken as written

explanation.surface: The bird first up gets the worms while its partner circles the nest diligently.
explanation.walkthrough: The first phrase rests on the proverb 'the early bird catches the worm'; 'circles' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something diligently and seriously is doing it with sincere application.

clue.text: Pound notes

parts.note: to hammer out notes on a guitar

explanation.surface: Paper money worth a pound each.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests old British banknotes; read pound as a verb, it is thrashing out chords on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a guitar by brushing the strings is to bang out chords.

clue.text: Mountaineer by arrangement provides detailed account

indicators.note: by arrangement means the letters of mountaineer are reordered

explanation.surface: A climber gives a full report as agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: A listing of items one by one is a detailed itemised account.
